checks.name: One four-wheel drive budget survives partial contacts, TCS and actual substep mechanical-work limits
Mechanical/electrical accounting remains physical during free spin and complete rigid-body takeoff/landing contact changes
Faster steering develops real tire-force curvature and yaw response on low/mid/high-speed circles and an authored city intersection
E/Q use the selected velocity immediately, brake smoothly on release and taper descent into real ground contact
G recovers level after manual pose changes and unsealed F arming, while real adhesion and finite thrust retain authority
New wheel, release-braking and recovery states preserve complete snapshot replay across display rates with seeded sensing and nozzle derating

driveBudget.policy: TCS on: normalized load shares, zero drive torque for unloaded wheels. TCS off: 25% torque and power per wheel, including airborne spin. No redistribution of unused power within a substep.
driveBudget.limiter: Analytic conservative midpoint-work bound from spin inertia and friction-circle contact torque; a small amount of rated power may remain unused.

contactAndEnergy.limits: The one-step partial-contact fixtures are deterministic load fixtures. This takeoff/landing trace is a separate full Cannon trajectory, not a curb-traversal claim. External gas compressor power is off-board.

steering.changes: Input-side lateral reference 0.9→1.0 g; inverse tanh lateral-slip compensation; steering lag 0.16→0.10 s and rack rate 1.25→1.8 rad/s. No direct pose/yaw writes, grip increase or yaw-force assist.
steering.tradeoff: A stronger full-key steering request causes more body slip; the high-speed radius remains constrained by tire force. The city test driver is confined to numerical validation and is not a gameplay shortcut.

verticalResponse.units: World vertical velocity m/s; requested command is independent of button hold duration.
verticalResponse.release: Finite force brakes velocity toward zero, then captures the achieved stop height.
verticalResponse.landing: Descent reference includes 3 m/s² stopping distance, 0.4 s feedback/valve allowance and a low-speed contact approach; contact still physically decides touchdown.

levelRecovery.diagnosis: Ordinary unsealed/off-F 3.8 numerical cases already levelled. The reproduced defect was suctionEnabled alone suppressing G at zero seal. A real sealed surface still suppresses aerial recovery. No body pose is assigned by G.

thrustAuthority.boundMeaning: independent-axis bounds; not simultaneously achievable, valve lag and allocation coupling remain
thrustAuthority.classification: All installed masses, inertias, nozzle layout and force ceilings are explicit engineering/playable-lab hypotheses. The gas law and nozzle thermodynamic relation are physics-based; no Tesla actuator calibration has been identified.

limits: Numerical physics and control validation only; no GPU-rendered driving feel, visuals or device FPS claim.
Rated thrust is deliberately unchanged. Finite gas, valve lag, asymmetric actuator failure, unilateral lift and coupled allocation remain physical limitations.
ABS is not ESC. The drive-power repair does not retune ABS to guarantee universal shorter stopping distances.
